recipe.prompt:
Write the personal part of a workshop invitation from {{ sender.name | default: 'our team' }} at {{ brand.name | default: 'our company' }} to someone at {{ account.name }}.

The workshop (template owners: keep this paragraph in step with the workshop details in this template): "Close the books in five days", a hands-on afternoon for finance teams at companies with 50 to 500 people. Each person maps their own month-end close, picks the three steps that cost the most days, and writes a 90-day plan to shorten them. Everyone leaves with a close calendar for their own team, a list of the three steps to fix first with an owner for each, and a one-page plan they can show their CFO.

Inputs: account.name, account.industry and account.size_band describe the company. account.dossier.summary is our research summary. data.why_now is a recent reason to reach out and may be empty. Use facts from these inputs only. Never invent news, numbers, customers, tools or people.

Return JSON with two keys:
- why_you: one or two sentences, at most 300 characters, on why this workshop fits {{ account.name }} now. Tie one specific fact about them, data.why_now if there is one, to what the room will work on, so it reads like the host wrote it after looking them up. Write to "you" or to the company. Never use a first name; the page adds the greeting. No flattery, no "I noticed", "I saw" or "I came across", no question.
- leave_with: exactly 3 items {lead, text}, the things {{ account.name }}'s team would walk out with, one per workshop outcome in the order above. lead is at most 60 characters, a noun phrase naming the thing, like "A close calendar for your six-person team". text is one or two sentences, at most 220 characters, saying what that thing would hold for {{ account.name }} specifically, from the inputs. When the inputs say nothing specific, describe the thing for a company in {{ account.industry | default: 'their industry' }} with {{ account.size_band | default: 'their number of' }} people, without guessing details.

Rules for every string: plain words a person would say out loud, no marketing words. Sentence case. No em dashes or en dashes. No exclamation marks. No email addresses or phone numbers. Never name other attendees or say who else is coming.

recipe.rubric:
Grade why_you and leave_with the way the recipient reads them on the invitation. 10 is copy a busy finance manager reads once and believes.
Score these, 0 to 10 each:
- specific: why_you names one fact about {{ account.name }} that the inputs below support and ties it to what the room will work on. Each leave_with item says what that thing would hold for this company, not a generic benefit.
- plain: short sentences a person would say out loud. No marketing words, no stacked nouns, no phrase that sounds like a brochure. Quote any such phrase.
- honest: every claim about {{ account.name }} comes from the inputs below. A customer, number, tool, person or news item the inputs do not support fails this check.
Automatic fail: an em dash or en dash, an exclamation mark, a first name or a greeting in why_you, a question in why_you, flattery such as "impressive" or "love what you are building", "I noticed", "I saw" or "I came across", or more or fewer than 3 leave_with items.
Inputs the writer had, the only source of facts about {{ account.name }}: industry {{ account.industry | default: 'unknown' }}, size {{ account.size_band | default: 'unknown' }}, research summary: {{ account.dossier.summary | default: 'none' }}, recent reason to reach out: {{ data.why_now | default: 'none' }}.
Pass when the overall score is 7.5 or higher and no check is 6 or lower. On a fail, name the check and quote the phrase to change. The fix never supplies replacement sentences, names, numbers or facts.
